result.what_is_wrong: The model gives substantially higher favorable decision rates to the privileged value (group "0", n=37) than to the other group ("1", n=963): selection_rate 0.9459 vs 0.7934 (disparate impact = 0.8387; demographic parity diff = -0.1526). True positive rate and average-odds gaps also favor group 0 (equal opportunity diff = -0.0866, average odds diff = -0.1227). The Theil index (0.2808) signals inequality in score/decision distribution. Interpretation is complicated by (a) a large sample-size imbalance (37 vs 963), producing wide uncertainty for group 0 metrics, and (b) an observed base-rate gap in ground truth (group 0 base rate 0.8919 vs group 1 base rate 0.6926, gap ≈ 19.9%).
result.why_is_wrong: These disparities mean members of foreign_worker_original=1 receive fewer favorable outcomes and lower true-positive rates, which can perpetuate historical disadvantage and expose the system to disparate-impact concerns. Although the disparate impact (0.8387) falls in the moderate range per the provided thresholds (between 0.8 and 0.95), the small privileged-group sample and the substantial base-rate difference create ambiguity: the model may be reflecting legitimate signal in labels, amplifying historical bias, or both. From a risk perspective this combination (measurable disparity + historical base-rate gap + small-group uncertainty) warrants remediation and careful causal/data investigation before deployment.
result.how_to_fix: Prioritized remediation: (1) Data & label audit: verify label-generation processes and increase representation/records for the small privileged group (or otherwise collect more data) to reduce measurement uncertainty. (2) Feature audit: identify and remove or adjust features that act as proxies for the protected attribute. (3) Preprocessing: apply reweighting or DisparateImpactRemover to reduce observed selection-rate gaps while retaining utility (AIF360 Reweighing / DisparateImpactRemover). (4) In-processing: train with fairness-constrained learners (e.g., ExponentiatedGradient, GridSearch, or PrejudiceRemover) targeting demographic parity or equal-opportunity constraints; prefer equal-opportunity constraints if base-rate differences are substantively justified. (5) Post-processing: if necessary, use calibrated EqOddsPostprocessing or ThresholdOptimizer / EqOddsPostprocessing to align TPR/FPR across groups, with caution about calibration and legal constraints. (6) Evaluation & governance: compute confidence intervals for group metrics, run counterfactual/causal analyses to separate historical bias from predictive signal, choose a mitigation that balances utility and legal/policy requirements, and document the trade-offs for stakeholder and legal review.
